messages:
alex: Heads-up, saw a spike in apiserver latency and controller-manager restarts in eu-west1 during a GPU node scale-up. etctd commit latency jumped and WAL fsync errors in node logs. Anyone actively watching?

maria: I saw alerts 12:04UTC, apiserver p95 went from 20ms -> 1.2s. controller-manager restarted twice in 6m.

dara: link: https://grafana.company.net/d/apiserver/eu-west1?panel=latency — spike lines up with a large `node-provision` job.

alex: copying a snippet from node where provisioning leaked io: ```May 10 12:03:45 node-33 kernel: INFO: task kubelet:... journal: fsync error: 5 (I/O error)
etcdwal: failed to write: write: short write
```

rui: etctd WAL I/O errors usually mean disk/ephemeral NVMe flapping or saturation. Which machine family?

maria: These were g4-family local NVMe. Provisioner started 24 pods that pulled large docker images simultaneously.

oncall-sre: infra-bot triggered auto-remediation: scaled down concurrent image pulls with `node.k8s.io/quiet-pulls=true` label on affected nodes. Tagged for follow-up. :white_check_mark:

alex: Good. We still saw controller-manager OOM/RestartCount increase. Could be backlog from API timeouts. Any throttling in kube-apiserver logs?

maria: kube-apiserver log excerpt: ```E0506 12:04:07 httputil.go:75] proxy error: net/http: request canceled (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)
W0506 12:04:10 controller.go:321] failed to sync: watch close: unexpected EOF```

dara: Two short-term mitigations: 1) reduce controller-manager `--concurrent-deployment-syncs` to 2 for this cluster to shrink reconciliation pressure, 2) temporarily lower image-pull burst by patching DaemonSet that manages provisioning to add `pod.spec.tolerations` to spread pulls.

rui: Agree. Also recommend moving etcd WAL to provisioned SSDs in that AZ or throttle fsync by tuning `--heartbeat-interval`? (would rather not). We should check cloud provider IOPS quotas.

alex: I'm going to perform controlled changes: patch controller-manager and add node label to pause aggressive pulls. Will monitor for 10m then revert if stable.

oncall-sre: ack. reminder: create follow-up ticket for storage sizing and add per-AZ IOPS limits to runbook.

maria: Quick cost note: moving WAL to provisioned SSD raises monthly costs ~+9% for that region but reduces incident MTTR. Documenting ROI in ticket.

dara: If we can't get more IOPS, fallback is to limit concurrent GPU attaches (we saw attach latency spike) which will throttle job startups but keep controlplane healthy.

alex: Done: patched controller-manager concurrency -> `--concurrent-deployment-syncs=2` and applied `node.k8s.io/quiet-pulls=true` to nodepool eu-west1-gpu-spot. Watching metrics.

infra-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-324, severity: medium, assigned: eng-sre, start_ts: 1768123456.

maria: 12:14UTC: p95 apiserver back to ~45ms, controller-manager stable, no new restarts. Good signal.

rui: Follow-ups: 1) check cloud provider quota history for the nodepool, 2) schedule test that injects heavy image pulls against a staging cluster to reproduce WAL saturation, 3) consider moving etcd backup/snapshot schedule to off-peak.

alex: I'll open tasks for those. Thanks all. If it resurfaces we'll escalate to infra eng and consider reserved NVMe for etcd and controlplane nodes. :thumbsup:
